title: Ingomar junior Mitchell Robbins meets Pontotoc Electric crews ahead of internship
excerpt: The local cooperative introduced Robbins to its crews Monday. His school district joined the regional IMPACTO career program in 2021.
locality: Pontotoc Electric Power Association in northeast Mississippi and Ingomar in Union County.

facts.statement: Mitchell Robbins, a junior at Ingomar, met Pontotoc Electric Power Association crews Monday morning as he prepared for his IMPACTO internship, the cooperative said. The utility serves part of Union County, where Ingomar is located, and all of Pontotoc and Ecru in neighboring Pontotoc County.
facts.evidence: PEPA’s dated post names the student, school, class year and purpose of the morning introduction. The utility lists both counties and the two incorporated cities as part of its service area. Union County participates in IMPACTO.
facts.date_context: Crew introduction Monday morning, Nov. 16, 2026. Program design and past placements are explicitly historical.
facts.locality: Pontotoc Electric Power Association in northeast Mississippi and Ingomar in Union County.
facts.identities: Mitchell Robbins, Pontotoc Electric Power Association, New Albany School District, Union County School District, Jacob Hogue and New Albany Light, Gas & Water.

facts.statement: New Albany schools started IMPACTO in 2018, and Union County schools joined in December 2021. The districts described a two-year track for juniors and seniors that pairs a career-readiness class with a 100-hour summer internship. Students could also pursue industry credentials or college credit.
facts.evidence: The district announcement records the launch and partnership dates, grade levels, two-year design, career readiness, optional industry certifications and dual enrollment, and a 100-hour summer project. These are program details as described in 2021.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell Robbins, a junior at Ingomar, met Pontotoc Electric Power Association crews Monday morning as he prepared for his IMPACTO internship, the cooperative said. The utility serves part of Union County, where Ingomar is located, and all of Pontotoc and Ecru in neighboring Pontotoc County.

New Albany schools started IMPACTO in 2018, and Union County schools joined in December 2021. The districts described a two-year track for juniors and seniors that pairs a career-readiness class with a 100-hour summer internship. Students could also pursue industry credentials or college credit.

The school district’s earlier intern profiles show what a utility placement has involved locally. At New Albany Light, Gas & Water, then-junior Jacob Hogue worked on rights of way and alongside crews responsible for repairs and construction.
